note: The verdicts are what the WRITTEN form demands (schema.json), what the site DOES at upload today, and what a READER derives. Where the three differ the case says so: that difference is the contract's tolerance, listed on purpose. `read` is the reader's view (the mod's, a Core's); `site` is what the door derives at upload — line count and tag bands — which counts the file as sent, before any reader normalises it.

cases.why: a lineage and one line is a file; everything else is optional
every key the current mod writes, read back as written — the whole file, none of it inherited
a file with no line has nothing to publish: a game set up a minute ago holds exactly this, and it must not become a catalogue row
a reader gives such a file a fresh lineage on its own machine; the site cannot — a lineage is what it files under
null and empty are the same capture: a line waiting for a translation, excluded from every score
S says the text was not in the source language; the value repeats the key so the game shows its own text, and the line is never asked again
the first format: a reader still takes it as a machine line and rewrites the file in the current form; the site refuses it at the door
a reader assumes a machine wrote it; a Core that writes it is refused at upload without warning — which is why it is written here
five letters, no sixth
an empty tag is not 'no tag': it is refused, where a missing one is read as A
i is omitted when absent, never null: a reader takes null as absent, the site refuses it
capture order starts at 1
the web editor sorts by it in JavaScript: above 2^53-1 the number is no longer exact
a line is {v, t, i} and nothing else in the written form; the site does not look at a fourth field, a reader drops it
M is the interface's tag: its lines live in modui-translate.json since 2026-09-04; a reader takes one found here out and rewrites, the site still accepts a file written before the split
LF only in the written form; every reader normalises CRLF in keys and values before anything else, and the hash is computed on that form — a Core that keeps CRLF has keys the site never finds
two keys that meet after normalisation are one line, and the one with the higher tag priority wins — a person over a review over a machine
a Core writes a lowercase GUID; the site's door still takes letters, digits and dashes up to 36 for files written before this was fixed — a tolerance, not the form
36 characters is what the site stores; beyond that the file was written and then the row failed
an empty lineage made whoever published it the Main of the lineage "" and every later one its branch
the uuid names a stored file; a step up is a folder chosen by the sender
a reader refuses the whole file rather than keep half of it (a fresh cache, not a wrong version); the site does not read this key
a block that is not an object reads as nothing; the site does not read this key at upload

a Core does not invent metadata; a reader leaves an underscore key it does not know alone when its value is not shaped like a line — neither a section nor a line: a newer writer's metadata — and so does the site

_One-quarter Brick Triangular Wall.v: Mur triangulaire d'un quart de brique
Mur triangulaire d'un quart de brique

cases.why: a game's text can begin with an underscore — a label found in a published translation, a signature line drawn with them. Metadata is the names of the schema and no other: read as metadata, such a line was written by the mod, dropped at the next load and sent to the model again at every launch, and never counted or published by the site
a mode is not an answer: a Core never writes it, a reader hands it over as stated and lets the language rule judge it
a string in the written form; a reader that meets a number reads its digits
the sections a file carries are read in file order and handed to their owners; a section absent from the file means this translation has none
_fonts is an object keyed by name, _exclusions a list: the written form fixes each container; a reader still hands the token to the owner, who yields an empty section
a file of the format 1 holds none of the new fields and is read, hashed and counted exactly as before: the format 2 is added to, never replaced
a term with two written forms, a sentence that links to it by form 1, and a sentence where a person said a word is NOT a term: all on lines, so each is one decision for the merge

a template reads two lists of the game; the entry that governs says its class in the template, the entry that follows says which form it takes for each class (0 = its own text); the value `[!L*quality=weapon]` carries neither
the file says it is format 1 and a line holds `term`: a reader of the format 1 would drop the field and the hash would not cover what the file says, so it is refused, never silently read
no `_engine_version` reads as format 1, so the same refusal holds when the file says nothing
in a format 1 file `[!g*0]` is the game's own text: nothing is asked of it, and the line is read as it always was
the text shows `[!g*0]` and the line holds no `links[0]`: a reader could only show the marker, which it never does, so the writer is refused
a link nothing points at would be kept for ever and counted « to read again » for nothing
the link names an entry that is no line of the file: it is refused when written (when read later, the sentence shows `was`)
the link asks for form 1 and the entry holds none: refused when written (when read later, the entry's translation is shown)
the template reads a list `_lists` does not hold: its slot could never be filled
the value shows an open slot the key never had: nothing says what text fills it
what a template takes from an entry must be a form the entry holds
a term whose own text shows a link marker would put the marker on the screen: it is refused, so no reader recurses
the entry a link points at must not show a marker either, whether or not it carries the term mark

a written form is LF only, like `v` and the keys: a file from elsewhere that holds a CR in one is NORMALISED on read (the same rule as v, common LineEndings), never refused — and what a WRITER of this library produces is refused (`guarantee`: the writer rule, asked of the raw text)
the `was` of a link is compared with what the link reads, and hashed as it is: LF only — read from elsewhere it is normalised first, a writer of this library never produces one
a line break is written LF: it is the text's own, and all that is asked is that nobody writes it another way
a person wrote the term their own way in this sentence and kept the link: `own` is that text, and it does not follow the term
an empty own writing says nothing: the field is simply absent
`by` is A or H
a link with no `was` can never be told « to read again » from a new one
`case` is upper-first or lower-first; another word is a newer writer's, not ours
a link is `{to, form, case, by, was}` and nothing else
`term` is written when true and never as false
form `0` is the entry's own `v` and is never listed
a form id is `f` and a canonical positive number: `f01` and `f1` would be one key twice
a form id starts with `f`: a key that looks like a number is turned into one by PHP arrays, sorted as one and re-encoded as a list
a template id is `t` and twelve hex digits (common TemplateIds): never a bare number, for the same reason
an id that is not of the derived shape cannot be one
`oracle` is one of accepted, refused, line, repeated-name
an empty list is not written: the field is simply absent
a person may say a word is not a term even where no line holds that term yet: nothing is checked against `unlinked`

the game's own tokens ride in `_lists`, in the ordinal order: the site counts the lines as before, a reader derives the same lines, and the content hash is the one it always was (`_lists` is not in it)
a file may know no token (an empty list is written as it is): `lists` stays required and may be empty
two extractions of one game must write the same bytes: an unsorted list is refused by a writer. The site's door does not read `_lists`, so it accepts it: a tolerance, listed on purpose
each token once: a repeat is not in strictly ascending order
an empty token would be found in every text
a token is the game's text, never a slot or a link: a marker in it is refused
the texts of the format 2 are LF alone

the same character is « Bo » in the family slot and « Bai » in the given-name slot of one template: `use` says what the template takes in the slots of each list (`ID:LIST`), the key of the whole template being the form every other slot takes
a key of `use` for a list `_lists` does not hold (« ghost ») has no slot to be read in: the template's own lists are all there
